title: Ghana's Finance Minister credits the Publican AI Trade Solution with over US$300 million in added customs assessments, after a pilot reported to have recovered GH¢15 million
summary: Ghana's Finance Minister reported that the Publican AI Trade Solution raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift.
account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. The platform analyzes trade data to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. MyJoy’s original launch report attributes GH¢15 million in recovered revenue from five companies to the pilot. The reports publish no recovery ledger. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments that took about two hours could be completed within five minutes. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. It describes the vendor only as a Cyprus-based firm. On 7 April 2026 the Member of Parliament for New Juaben South called for the system's suspension, and MyJoyOnline reported that a coalition of traders and freight forwarders demanded the same. Some importers reported duty assessments rising from about GH¢900,000 to over GH¢2.1 million. On 22 April 2026 a welfare officer of the Ghana Union of Traders Association said that some traders were reportedly paying up to 300% more in duties than before. The next day a Customs Laboratory official of the authority said that officers review the system's suggested values and set them aside when importers prove their prices. In the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review of 23 July 2026, Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson reported that Publican raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. On 9 August 2026 MyJoyOnline reported that the Commissioner-General said that monthly customs revenue had averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system and reached GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.
purpose: The Ghana Revenue Authority deployed the system to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation, and to give full coverage of customs assessment.
developer: A Cyprus-based firm that the Ghanaian Times does not name
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: The Finance Minister reports that assessed customs collections rose by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. That is a measured gain in the Ghana Revenue Authority's result. The government counted it itself, and traders dispute it.
No source traces the added revenue to public spending or other wider effects.

ai_role.statement: The Finance Ministry counts the system's contribution as the gap between importers' declared values and the assessed values. The system analyzed about 366,000 declarations, and 24 percent triggered more than one valuation risk indicator for review by customs officers. Officers review its suggested values, and importers who object with documents such as bank records or contracts can have them set aside. No source separates the system's flags from the officers' decisions, and the count is the deployer's own.

display.answer: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry summarizes Ghanaian reports of the launch, including MyJoy's report of the GH¢15 million recovery. The US$300 million figure comes from the Finance Minister's mid-year review, and the July revenue figure comes from the Commissioner-General through MyJoyOnline. fields.summary: Ghana's Finance Minister reported that the Publican AI Trade Solution raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift.
fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. The platform analyzes trade data to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. MyJoy’s original launch report attributes GH¢15 million in recovered revenue from five companies to the pilot. The reports publish no recovery ledger. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments that took about two hours could be completed within five minutes. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. It describes the vendor only as a Cyprus-based firm. On 7 April 2026 the Member of Parliament for New Juaben South called for the system's suspension, and MyJoyOnline reported that a coalition of traders and freight forwarders demanded the same. Some importers reported duty assessments rising from about GH¢900,000 to over GH¢2.1 million. On 22 April 2026 a welfare officer of the Ghana Union of Traders Association said that some traders were reportedly paying up to 300% more in duties than before. The next day a Customs Laboratory official of the authority said that officers review the system's suggested values and set them aside when importers prove their prices. In the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review of 23 July 2026, Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson reported that Publican raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. On 9 August 2026 MyJoyOnline reported that the Commissioner-General said that monthly customs revenue had averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system and reached GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.
